openGraph.title: Samarth Nagar — Software Engineer
openGraph.description: Software engineer building APIs, real-time systems, and developer tools with TypeScript, Node.js, and Go.

points: Most of the work was on a product that generated static assets on a server and stored them in S3. I moved generation into the browser, so assets are made only when someone asks for one. That removed the server-side inference work and the storage bucket it depended on, and with them the recurring cost.

Helped move Supabase from a managed hosted plan to a self-hosted deployment running in Docker. It took more setup, but the team got control over the environment and stopped running into the limits that came with the hosted plan.

Spent a lot of time in the database layer: changed schemas, migrated existing tables, and updated the authentication flow that relied on them. I also added caching in the Next.js app, which brought p90 cold starts down by up to about 500 ms.

Reviewed roughly 118 API endpoints and checked database integrity, using Postman and AI-assisted tooling to find problems. I worked with the rest of the team to fix what we found rather than just writing it down.
Built an internal code-generation pipeline for the asset workflow, so the repetitive part of that work stopped being manual.
Built and improved dashboards, forms, and shared UI components in React so the internal tools were easier to use day to day.
Worked directly with non-technical colleagues to understand what they actually needed, explain the trade-offs in plain language, and turn those conversations into changes in the product.

items.title: Cloud Workspace
items.desc: A shared workspace for small teams: messaging, group chats, tasks, files, and meetings in one place. Chat runs over WebSockets backed by Cloudflare Durable Objects, with a REST and polling fallback so it keeps working when sockets drop. Sign-in, workspace roles, and token handling use Better Auth.

items.title: SQL Visualizer
items.desc: Paste PostgreSQL DDL and get an interactive ER diagram. It reads tables, keys, and constraints — including schema-qualified names and foreign keys — and lays them out so you can actually see how the schema fits together. Export the result as PNG or SVG.

items.title: Local AI Assistant
items.desc: A chat UI for Ollama models running on your own machine. Responses stream token by token, installed models are detected automatically, and conversation history stays in your browser. No account, no API key, and no data sent to a cloud provider.

items.title: Personal Blog Platform
items.desc: A place for longer posts, short thoughts, and weekly logs. Content lives in MDX files, so publishing is a git push rather than a trip through a CMS. Search, code highlighting, and a theme toggle are built in.

items.title: Client-Side Video Processing
items.desc: Convert, resize, compress, and trim video in the browser with ffmpeg.wasm. Files are never uploaded — all processing happens locally, including GIF palette optimization and multithreading where the browser supports it.

items.title: Live Token Meter
items.desc: An OpenCode plugin that shows live tokens per second, usage from the last response, and session totals in the CLI footer. Published on npm. The live estimate settles against the provider's actual usage numbers once a response finishes.

items.title: Single Sign-On Service
items.desc: A small sign-on service built from scratch: bcrypt-hashed passwords, expiring JWTs, and middleware that protects every route except signup and signin. No off-the-shelf auth library doing the work behind the scenes.

items.title: Dotfiles & Dev Environment
items.desc: A terminal-first Linux setup built around Neovim, tmux, fish, and Lazygit. It is the daily driver I use for systems and backend work, kept in version control so a fresh machine is a few commands away.

items.title: goshell
items.desc: A minimal shell in Go built with the standard library. It runs external programs and multi-stage pipelines by connecting processes with os.Pipe, and includes cd, exit, and history built-ins with !! and !n re-execution.

blog.title: Blog & Notes
blog.desc: Long-form posts, short thoughts, and weekly logs on software engineering, systems, and developer tools.

research.title: Research
research.body: Analyzed the real production codebase behind react.dev to map architecture decisions: custom MDX components, a build-time SSG pipeline, and the React Compiler already running in production.
points: No state management library needed — URL + useState + Context sufficient
50+ custom MDX components behind each doc page
Custom SSG pipeline that serializes React tree to JSON at build time
Build-time eval() workarounds acknowledged as intentional hacks
